claims.value: Toreno gives side B 12,000 assigned to San Juan for the pass; a separate advance guard was posted at Sepúlveda.
claims.rationale: Assignment for pass defence, before the later detachment/retreat sequence; not necessarily the same population as all still at the pass on the battle morning. English rendering (ours): "12,000 men and some guns in all."

claims.value: Napoleon’s evening letter gives 9,000 opponents occupying Somosierra.
claims.rationale: Opponent estimate after action, not a French own-force figure. The following separate Sepúlveda force is not included. English rendering (ours): "A corps of 9,000 men occupied Somosierra."

citations.locator: napoleon-t18, printed p. 86, Internet Archive leaf 95; inspected page-image excerpt

claims.value: The subsequent French bulletin gives 13,000 Spanish reserve troops defending the pass.
claims.rationale: Same official French publication family, different document and date; not independent corroboration or an averaged estimate. English rendering (ours): "A division of 13,000 Spanish reserve troops defended the mountain passage."

citations.locator: napoleon-t18, printed p. 87, Internet Archive leaf 96; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Une division de 13,000 hommes de l’armée de réserve espagnole défendait le passage de cette montagne.

claims.value: Toreno puts San Juan’s assignment under the Central Junta’s defence arrangements directed through Morla and Castelar.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "After Burgos the Central Junta entrusted Morla and Castelar with defending Madrid and the Guadarrama, Fonfría, Navacerrada and Somosierra passes."

citations.locator: toreno-t2, printed p. 166, Internet Archive leaf 171; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: La junta central después de la rota de Burgos habia encargado á Don Tomás de Morla y al marqués de Castelar atendiesen á la defensa de Madrid, y de los pasos de Guadarrama, Fonfria, Navacerrada y Somosierra.

claims.value: The French bulletin credits Montbrun with leading the Polish Guard charge.
claims.rationale: Retains the bulletin’s attributed command and causal rhetoric without treating it as an established effect or reconciling other possible charge leaders. English rendering (ours): "A charge by General Montbrun at the head of the Polish Guard light cavalry decided the affair."

claims.value: Toreno reports an order to gallop up the road in reaction to resistance; the quoted pronoun does not itself identify a subordinate charge leader.
claims.rationale: The continuation names the Polish lancers; Bodart names Napoleon. The page is retained in full. English rendering (ours): "Irritated and impatient with the resistance, he then ordered a galloping charge up the road."

open_questions: Reconcile pass defenders versus detached Sepúlveda troops and the differing French dispatch/bulletin estimates; identify the actual Polish charge command from reports.
Deferred: the dated original returns and reports identified above, and any deeper source-lineage reconciliation. No additional research cycle follows merely from this gap.

Source dependence: Bodart is a later compilation. Toreno, Foy, Oman, Saint-Cyr and the official Correspondance are interested or retrospective source families, and embedded/reprinted reports are not extra independent witnesses. Agreement does not establish independence.

A.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Source-specific alternatives below retain their own moment and population. Alternatives/limits: No comparable own-force French return for the actual attacking force was established in the letters/bulletin read. Regimental names, loss figures and enemy estimates do not supply it.
A.command_scope: Printed side-A commander Napoleon; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. The French bulletin credits Montbrun with leading the Polish Guard charge.
A.army_continuity: Unknown: these passages do not establish a cross-engagement army identity.

B.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Civilians, recruits, regular troops and surrender survivors are not interchangeable. Alternatives/limits: Toreno gives side B 12,000 assigned to San Juan for the pass; a separate advance guard was posted at Sepúlveda. Napoleon’s evening letter gives 9,000 opponents occupying Somosierra. The subsequent French bulletin gives 13,000 Spanish reserve troops defending the pass.
B.command_scope: Printed side-B commander Benito de San-Juan; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Toreno puts San Juan’s assignment under the Central Junta’s defence arrangements directed through Morla and Castelar.
B.army_continuity: Unknown: repeated names and formation labels do not establish continuity.
